summary: The Excellence Scholarships of the Government of Mexico for Foreigners are run by AMEXCID, part of Mexico's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. They support full-time, in-person study or research at about 90 to 100 participating Mexican higher education and research institutions. The 2026 call covers undergraduate and master's mobility (exchange) periods, full master's degrees, and doctoral and postdoctoral research stays for nationals of more than 170 countries. Awards give a monthly stipend, tuition and enrolment fees as set by each institution, health insurance from the seventh month, a visa fee exemption and some transport costs.
eligibility_notes:
The call is open to nationals of the countries listed in Annex 5 of the call (over 170 countries, under bilateral agreements, multilateral mechanisms and special agreements). People with more than one nationality send one single application, under one of the eligible nationalities, the one they will be accredited with. Only one application per person is accepted; a duplicate is disqualified automatically. Applications must be written in Spanish.

Study types: undergraduate mobility and master's mobility (up to 12 months), a full master's degree (up to 24 months), and doctoral or postdoctoral research fellowships (6 to 12 months). All must be full-time and in person. Applications are accepted only for the institutions in Annex 1. Scholarships begin between August and before 10 November 2026 and last at least 6 months.

Academic results: for exchange (mobility) and master's applicants, the host university's acceptance letter must state a grade average of 85 on a 0 to 100 scale (8.5 on a 10 scale), and a master's applicant's own transcript must also show at least that average. Doctoral and postdoctoral applicants need a doctoral degree, an acceptance letter that names a supervisor and the research project title, and a nomination letter from an academic or governmental institution.

Language: if your native language is not Spanish, you must present a certificate at level B2 or higher of the Common European Framework. If the programme is taught in a language other than Spanish and different from your native language, the host institution must send a letter promising advising or tutoring in that language.

Not eligible: foreign diplomats accredited in Mexico and their immediate family; foreigners living in Mexico without a Temporary Resident Student card; foreigners who also hold Mexican nationality, including children of Mexican parents; people with a Mexican family reunification visa or who aim to obtain one; people who got a scholarship from any federal government institution in the immediately preceding year; people who hold a scholarship from any Mexican government agency; former AMEXCID scholars who have not yet let the same number of months pass since their scholarship; former AMEXCID scholars who did not successfully finish an earlier award; people under 18 at the time of application; and people who live in a country other than their country of nationality, or who have the support, recommendation or sponsorship of institutions outside their country of origin. No scholarship is given for writing a thesis to finish a degree.
age_experience_notes: Minimum age is 18 at the time of application; if your passport was issued before you turned 18, update it. For doctoral and postdoctoral research stays, the evaluation looks at awards and honours, extra specialised training and related professional experience, teaching experience (years of service, full-time or part-time), and at least one year in leadership roles in university administration or public research institutions. No maximum age is stated.
funding_summary: For master's, undergraduate mobility and master's mobility the monthly stipend is four times the UMA, currently MXN 14,264.88; for doctoral and postdoctoral research stays it is five times the UMA, currently MXN 17,831.10. Both are paid monthly in arrears, and the UMA can change by law. The award also pays enrolment and tuition fees as each institution's programme sets them, IMSS health insurance from the seventh month, a Mexican visa fee exemption, economy airfare on successful completion for eligible countries, and domestic transport when studying outside Mexico City. The scholarship lasts up to 12 months (mobility), up to 24 months (master's) or 6 to 12 months (research stays), and cannot be deferred to later academic years. It depends on AMEXCID's budget availability.
programmes_note: The call does not list individual programmes. Programmes must be full-time and in person at the institutions of Annex 1; the participating institutions have programmes registered in Mexico's national postgraduate system. The applicant system has a section that shows all participating institutions and the programmes they offer. Selection gives preference to research on: sustainable food systems and nutrition; ending discrimination and violence against women and girls; water management and sanitation; renewable energy and clean energy access; social, economic and political inequalities and human rights; sustainable consumption and waste reduction; climate change mitigation and adaptation; and protection and sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, biodiversity and forests. A thesis-writing scholarship to complete a degree is not offered.
institutions_note: The programme page says 90 Mexican higher education institutions take part; the Annex 1 list of the 2026 call numbers about 100 entries. Institutions named include: Benemerita Universidad Autonoma de Puebla (BUAP); CICESE; CIAD; CentroGeo; CIMAT; CIMAV; CIQA; CINVESTAV; CIDE; CIESAS; CIBNOR; CIO; CIMMYT; Colegio de Posgraduados; El Colegio de Mexico; El Colegio de Michoacan; El Colegio de la Frontera Norte and Sur; El Colegio de Jalisco, San Luis, Tlaxcala and Mexiquense; FLACSO; Instituto Mora; IMTA; INAH; INAOE; INEEL; INMEGEN; ININ; INSP; Instituto Politecnico Nacional; ITAM; many Tecnologicos (Aguascalientes, Cd. Victoria, Celaya, Chetumal, Colima, Conkal, Culiacan, Durango, La Paz, Merida, Morelia, Nuevo Leon, Tuxtla Gutierrez, Veracruz and others); Tecnologico de Monterrey (Campus Monterrey); Instituto Tecnologico y de Estudios Superiores de Occidente; Universidad Autonoma de Aguascalientes, Baja California, Chapingo, Chiapas, Chihuahua, Ciudad Juarez, Coahuila, Guadalajara, Nuevo Leon, Queretaro, San Luis Potosi, Sinaloa, Tamaulipas, Tlaxcala, Yucatan, Zacatecas, Hidalgo, Estado de Mexico and Metropolitana (UAM); Universidad de Colima, Guadalajara, Monterrey; Universidad Iberoamericana CDMX; Universidad La Salle Mexico; Universidad Michoacana; UNAM; Universidad Pedagogica Nacional; Universidad Veracruzana; UPAEP; and several polytechnic and technological universities. You pick the host institution yourself and need its acceptance letter; the institution has the final say on admission.

summary.detail: Undergraduate mobility only: an exchange period of up to 12 months at a Mexican institution, full-time and in person. A full bachelor's degree in Mexico is not offered by this call. Needs host acceptance letter with grade average of 85/100, a letter from the home institution agreeing to recognise the credits, and grades for the last completed period.

Two options: master's mobility (exchange, up to 12 months) and a full master's degree (up to 24 months). Stipend is 4 times the UMA (MXN 14,264.88 per month). Needs the bachelor's degree, the transcript of the latest semester with an average of 85/100, and the host acceptance letter (issued within 60 calendar days) stating the same average and programme dates. No thesis-writing-only scholarships.

Doctoral research fellowship (research stay) of 6 to 12 months, not a full doctoral degree. Stipend is 5 times the UMA (MXN 17,831.10 per month). Needs a doctoral degree, a host acceptance letter naming the supervisor and research project title, a nomination letter from an academic or governmental institution, and Form 3 project description.
Postdoctoral research fellowship of 6 to 12 months. Same stipend (5 times the UMA, MXN 17,831.10 per month) and same documents as the doctoral research stay.

benefits.limit_text: MXN 14,264.88 per month (4 times the UMA) for master's, undergraduate mobility and master's mobility
benefits.conditions: Paid monthly in arrears, at the end of the month, as AMEXCID indicates. The UMA value is subject to changes by law.

benefits.limit_text: MXN 17,831.10 per month (5 times the UMA) for doctoral and postdoctoral research fellowships
benefits.conditions: Paid monthly in arrears. The UMA value is subject to changes by law.

benefits.limit_text: Enrolment and tuition fees as set by each Mexican institution's programme
benefits.conditions: Subject to the final decision of each institution, as stated in the acceptance letter issued to the applicant.

benefits.limit_text: Health insurance from the Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS), family insurance modality; starts in the seventh month of the scholarship and lasts a period similar to the scholarship
benefits.conditions: Covers medical, surgical, pharmaceutical, hospital care and maternity. Not covered: cosmetic surgery, glasses, contact lenses and hearing aids, surgery to correct sight defects, self-inflicted injuries, injuries from risky sports, preventive check-ups, behaviour and learning disorder treatment, dental treatment except extractions, fillings and cleaning, orthoses and prostheses, and fertility treatment. Pre-existing conditions and waiting periods apply. Until cover starts, the scholar pays own medical costs; the call recommends buying international health insurance for that period.

benefits.limit_text: Exemption from Mexican visa issuance fees
benefits.conditions: Anyone staying 180 days or more must get the visa specified by the Office of Academic Exchange from a Mexican embassy or consulate abroad.

benefits.limit_text: International economy-class airfare on successful completion of the scholarship, on the route AMEXCID judges most convenient
benefits.conditions: Only for the 111 countries listed in Annex 3 (Canada, Chile, Suriname, 53 African countries, 18 in Asia, 11 in the Caribbean, 6 in Europe, 6 in the Middle East and 14 in the Pacific). AMEXCID buys the ticket; tickets bought by the scholar are not reimbursed; changes to the ticket after issue are the scholar's cost. A scholar who does not use the ticket may ask for reimbursement of expenses incurred.

benefits.limit_text: Domestic transport from Mexico City to the host city and back, when studying outside Mexico City
benefits.conditions: Only after all academic requirements are completed; either domestic air or ground transport, depending on the institution (Annex 4). For ground travel the scholar pays for the bus ticket and is reimbursed.

benefits.limit_text: Any expense not named in the call is not covered or reimbursed
benefits.conditions: The call advises having enough funds for at least the first 60 days.

requirements.text: Copy of a valid passport showing identification data. Update the passport if it was issued before you turned 18.
Declaration letter, typed and signed by the applicant (Form 1).
CV, typed, maximum 4 pages, signed by the applicant (Form 2).
Medical certificate from a public or private health institution, issued no more than 3 months before applying, stating the applicant is in good health. If not in Spanish, add a certified translation.
Certificate of Spanish at level B2 or higher of the Common European Framework.
requirements.conditional_rule: if your native language is not Spanish

requirements.text: Academic documents relevant to the type of study or research (the call asks for these in addition to the list above).

Acceptance letter from the host university, issued no more than 60 calendar days earlier, stating a grade average of 85/100 (8.5/10) and the start and end dates of the programme. The letter needs the institution's letterhead, the name and signature of the issuing authority, duration with dates as DD/MM/YYYY, type of study, name of the academic programme, and the campus and state; for research stays also the full name of the research project.
requirements.conditional_rule: undergraduate and master's mobility, and master's degree applicants

requirements.text: Letter from the home institution agreeing to recognise or transfer the credits of the courses taken in Mexico.

requirements.conditional_rule: master's mobility and master's degree applicants

requirements.text: Grades for the last period completed, issued by the home institution. For a master's degree, the transcript of the most recent semester must show an average of at least 85/100 (8.5/10).
Letter from the host institution committing to advising or tutoring in another language, naming the language and the advisor or tutor.
requirements.conditional_rule: if the programme is taught in a language other than Spanish and other than your native language

requirements.text: Acceptance letter from the research institution stating that supervision will be given, the supervisor's name and the research project title.
Nomination letter from an academic or governmental institution (according to your nationality) stating the research to be carried out and the reason for the nomination.

Format rules: documents not in Spanish need a simple Spanish translation on a separate sheet signed by the applicant; files are colour PDFs of at most 1.8 MB, legible; signatures must match the passport and be in blue ink; all documents must be attached in the system before the deadline. AMEXCID staff do not change data or accept paper or outside files.
A current photo is uploaded in the registration form (jpg, jpeg, png, bmp or gif, at the size the system shows).

application_steps.title: Prepare documents and get a host institution acceptance letter
application_steps.detail: Choose a full-time, in-person programme at an institution in Annex 1 and obtain its acceptance letter (issued within 60 calendar days of applying). Prepare Forms 1, 2 and, for research stays, 3, plus passport, medical certificate, degree, transcript and Spanish B2 certificate if needed. Documents not in Spanish need a signed Spanish translation; each file must be a colour PDF of at most 1.8 MB.

application_steps.title: Register in the SIGCA academic cooperation system
application_steps.detail: Create a user in the SIGCA system with your e-mail address and password (the manual says to use Google Chrome). In the available calls section open the call for your country, then fill in every field marked with a red asterisk, upload a current photo and the documents. You can save the draft at any time; saving alone does not send the application.

application_steps.title: Submit the single application before the deadline
application_steps.detail: Press the apply button once everything is complete; after sending, data and documents cannot be changed. The 2026 system opened at 6:00 p.m. on 21 May 2026 and closed at 3:00 p.m. on 22 June 2026, Central Mexico Time. Only one application per person is allowed, in Spanish; duplicates are disqualified. A person with several nationalities applies once under one eligible nationality. Questions about registration go to the call's e-mail address, which answers only registration questions.

application_steps.title: AMEXCID selects candidates using set criteria
application_steps.detail: Criteria are: all required documents submitted; distribution of scholarships by country; academic excellence record; preference for people who never held an AMEXCID scholarship; order of submission (earlier applications are preferred); and distribution by receiving institution. For research stays, awards, extra training, professional and teaching experience and leadership experience are also assessed, and topics listed in the call (food, gender equality, water, clean energy, inequality, sustainable consumption, climate, ecosystems) get preference. Admission to an institution does not guarantee a scholarship.

application_steps.title: Results are sent by e-mail to selected candidates only
application_steps.detail: In 2026, selected candidates were told between 6 and 10 July 2026. If you get no message, you were not selected. Decisions are final and rejected applications get no answer. The final decision rests only with the Government of Mexico. If a selected candidate does not confirm acceptance, AMEXCID may give the award to another candidate.

application_steps.title: Formalise the scholarship and accept its terms
application_steps.detail: Selected candidates get instructions by e-mail on how to formalise the award, and must send their acceptance to AMEXCID; no answer in the set time can cancel the award. By accepting, the scholar agrees to follow the Rules Applicable to Foreign Scholarship Recipients and any updates. AMEXCID's scholarship office explains payment and travel administration before formalisation.

application_steps.title: Get the visa, start studies and report in Mexico City
application_steps.detail: Anyone staying 180 days or more must obtain the specified visa from a Mexican embassy or consulate abroad (fees are exempt). Studies or research must begin between August and 10 November 2026 or the scholarship is revoked. The scholar must report to the AMEXCID academic exchange office in Mexico City within the first 10 calendar days of the first month, on the date staff give. No changes of programme, institution or project, and no extension or deferral, are allowed after the award.

application_steps.title: Receive payments and completion travel
application_steps.detail: The stipend is paid monthly in arrears. Health insurance begins in the seventh month; the scholar covers medical costs before then. AMEXCID buys the return airfare (for eligible countries) and the domestic transport only after the scholar completes all academic requirements.
